How the calculation works

Required remaining average = (Target − Earned course contribution) ÷ (1 − Completed weight / 100)

A worked example

Completed work covers 60% of the course and has contributed 45 percentage points. To finish at 80%, the remaining 40% must supply 35 points: 35 ÷ 0.40 = 87.50%.

Before you use the result

Enter the contribution to the full course, not your normalized current average. For example, 75% on completed work worth 60% contributes 45 points. The completed contribution cannot exceed the completed weight. All remaining work is modeled as one combined average; category-specific pass rules are not applied.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

What is an earned course contribution?

Multiply each completed score by its course weight, then add the results. A score of 80% worth 25% contributes 20 percentage points.

Can the remaining work contain several assessments?

Yes. The answer is the combined weighted average required across that work, not a required score for every individual assessment.
